title_original: Nutrients in our food are declining. Can regenerative agriculture save it?
summary_source: Approach focuses on rebuilding soil health, increasing biodiversity and restoring natural ecosystems For the last few decades, the nutrient content of our crops has been declining. In the late 90s, the US Department of Agriculture found the vitamin C content of lemons had decreased by almost a third over the previous 22 years. Calcium in carrots, an important source especially for non-meat eaters, had reduced , on average, by more than a quarter. Vitamin A in bananas was down by 57%. The mineral content of wheat has declined by between 20-30% since the 1960s. A number of reasons have been suggested for this worrying decline, ranging from new varieties of crop that are bred to grow quicker and bigger to the higher carbon dioxide levels in the air causing plants to produce more sugars and starches (they grow faster but they produce fewer nutrients). A wide range of fixes have been suggested, from GM crops to synthetic soil amendments, or underground farms. Continue reading...

Sign up here The ocean waters around the Galápagos Islands are hot. Very hot. Observed for centuries in the Pacific by fishers, the El Niño weather phenomenon begins when the prevailing trade winds slow, allowing warm water to spread east along the coast of South America. This summer, high temperatures have become inescapable. People have coped with makeshift solutions: keeping curtains drawn, placing foil over windows or – for those who can afford one – plugging in an air-conditioning unit. In 2023, after years of coping with the noxious odors, Kyereh began collecting air samples in her yard for a local environmental justice group. But soon after, Louisiana passed an industry-backed law that sharply restricted how that kind of data could be used. Ten of Louisiana’s heaviest air-polluting facilities, based on self-reported data shared with the EPA, operate without a single public air monitor within five miles. This list includes Dow Chemical’s plastics factory in Plaquemine, which is about eight miles from the nearest air monitoring station. The station measures only ozone even though the plant releases an array of toxic pollutants including ethylene oxide, a known carcinogen. title_original: Kemi declares war on net zero – and what remains of her party
summary_source: Badenoch’s ideological purge gathers pace as moderates are cast out and the Tories edge ever closer to political extinction You have to hand it to Kemi Badenoch. She doesn’t take any prisoners. While the rest of us have been trying to survive a heatwave and are wondering if air-con may be needed for future summers, the Tory leader has taken a more hardline approach to climate change. Call it Schrödinger’s climate change. It’s both happening and not happening at the same time. Kemi is just about sane enough not to be an out-and-out denier. She leaves that to Reform. Mind you, no one would put it past her to suggest the scientists have got it wrong if the temperature drops for a few days. title_original: Carbon markets alone won’t keep Southeast Asia’s forests standing, study says
summary_source: - A new study has identified “massive and untapped” conservation potential within forestry and plantation concessions in Southeast Asia. - Roughly 42 million hectares of forests remain standing inside logging, oil palm, timber and rubber plantation concessions across the region, the study says. - The researchers examined what it would take to financially incentivize forest conservation inside these concessions, finding that using carbon markets alone would require carbon prices many times higher than current values. - They point to the need for diversified sources of conservation funding to complement carbon markets, such as blended finance, green bonds and payment for ecosystems services, as well as more supportive governance frameworks that elevate the viability of conservation over development.

summary_source: Weather system tied to warming sea surface expected to intensify in fall and winter, persisting until early spring 2027 El Niño , a recurring climate phenomenon marked by above-average sea surface temperatures, when changes in wind patterns allow warmer water to spread across the central and eastern equatorial Pacific, could spell a wet winter for portions of the western and south-eastern US, climate models show. Coastal areas may be at elevated risk of flooding, experts warn. Climate scientists predict this year’s “super” El Niño, a label assigned when sea surface temperatures climb by at least 2C , will be the strongest of the century. The weather system is expected to intensify in the fall and winter, persisting until early spring 2027, according to the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa). title_original: Amazon deforestation alerts fall to lowest level since 2013, Brazilian data show
summary_source: - INPE’s DETER system recorded 2,874 sq km of Amazon deforestation alerts from August 2025 through July 2026, down 36% from the previous year and 55.6% below the preceding 10-year average. - The total is the lowest since 2013 when earlier DETER data are included. If the trend is confirmed by the higher-resolution PRODES system, Brazil could record its lowest official Amazon deforestation rate since monitoring began in 1988. - The decline has coincided with stronger environmental enforcement under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Alerts also fell in the Cerrado, Caatinga, Atlantic Forest, and Pampa, with the Cerrado reaching a five-year low. - Despite the decline in clear-cutting, the Amazon remains vulnerable to logging, drought, forest degradation, and fire, which can cause substantial ecological damage without immediately appearing in deforestation statistics.

title_original: The Guardian view on India’s green growth gamble: it will need more than private finance | Editorial
summary_source: The world’s most populous country needs state-generated demand to industrialise, decarbonise and avoid China’s overcapacity trap India is attempting to do something the world has never seen before. So claimed Niti Aayog, the government of India’s policy thinktank, earlier this year. It said that no major economy has tried to expand GDP nearly eightfold within a generation while simultaneously redirecting its energy and industrial systems to reach net zero within two generations. Hence its detailed report ’s claim that there is “no historical precedent”. There is something to this. China industrialised at vast scale, but not on a sustainable net zero path. Korea, Japan and Europe became wealthy by industrialising before decarbonising. Today, rich nations have already satisfied the basic demands of their people and created the infrastructure and high per-capita energy use that India is still trying to build. title_original: Indonesia’s wildfire season surges as haze spreads into Malaysia
summary_source: - Fires in Indonesia’s West Kalimantan province have sent haze across the border into Malaysia, where worsening air pollution has forced six schools in Sarawak state to switch to online classes. - Indonesia is entering the peak of its fire season, with West Kalimantan accounting for more than half of the nearly 49,000 hectares (121,000 acres) burned across six priority provinces as of Aug. 9. - The fires are also threatening biodiversity, including orangutan habitat and rehabilitation efforts in West Kalimantan, while a separate blaze has forced the closure of Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park on the island of Java. - Authorities have deployed tens of thousands of personnel and dozens of aircraft to fight the fires, but environmental groups say funding cuts and the intensifying El Niño are raising concerns about Indonesia’s preparedness.

title_original: How can we talk about this extreme weather now that it’s a battleground in the culture wars? | Andy Beckett
summary_source: Weather forecasts once gave Britons something safe to chat about. Not any more, and that’s a problem for the experts – indeed, for all of us In this fragmented but supposedly mild country, watching and talking about the weather forecast is meant to be a reassuring, unifying activity. Collectively, we have created and maintained a national climate narrative of small disappointments and pleasures. The first weather forecaster to appear on British TV, George Cowling, made his debut on the BBC in January 1954, predicting that “tomorrow would be rather windy”, but “a good day to hang out the washing”. For most of the 72 years since, such brief, carefully calibrated broadcasts have provided people from Aberdeen to Penzance with practical information, small talk and minor grumbles about essentially the same situation: living in a country where the weather is constantly changing, in a paradoxically unchanging way. title_original: New studies portray Amazon as surprisingly resilient, but tipping point looms
summary_source: - Three 2026 studies reveal that the Amazon can regrow quickly, but deforestation and warming could trigger a system-wide tipping point in the next 15 years. - Research also shows that repeated wildfires are replacing fire-resistant specialist trees with generalist species, halving biodiversity at forest edges despite a closing canopy. - According to research, extreme conditions have increased tree mortality due to hydraulic failure, which is key to understanding the forest’s shrinking carbon sinks. - Ending deforestation is necessary and achievable, but must be combined with global actions to curb climate change, say experts.

summary_source: Many complained online that piercingly loud tone was ‘overreach’ while others lamented lack of action on decarbonisation On Friday at 7pm, Thérèse Coffey was nine miles away from a nuclear power station when her phone made a loud, piercing and very worrying sound: it was a “severe” emergency alert . “Was expecting [a] much more specific alert, not a generic message on wildfires,” the former Conservative cabinet minister said on X. She wasn’t alone in being alarmed by the alarm sent to phones in England and Wales. In the aftermath, thousands of social media users expressed their shock at the alert. Some shared funny memes and others lamented what they viewed as lack of government action on decarbonisation. Academic John Ritzema called it a “massive overreach” and said the alert system should be “for ‘drop everything and prepare for something terrible’ situations”, something Coffey echoed, saying alerts should not become commonplace to avoid “Peter cries wolf situations”. title_original: Destroyed crops, riverbed cyclists and a ‘Rock of Starvation’: how drought has devastated the Danube
summary_source: The Guardian travelled 100 miles along the EU’s longest river, where some residents are struggling to secure drinking water For centuries, the rock was seen as a warning. When it began to emerge from the Danube, beneath Gellért Hill in Budapest, it meant the river had fallen so low that floating mills could no longer operate, crops were probably failing, and hunger would almost certainly follow. That is why, in the Hungarian capital, where over time the boulder became little more than a legend, it was named Ínség-szikla – the Rock of Starvation. Today, amid record-low water levels on the Danube, the rock has not only emerged from the water, but surfaced almost in its entirety, along with the sandy riverbed on which it rests, astonishing geologists and government scientists sent to examine it. And, much as the rock was said to warn, Hungary is now facing an unprecedented energy crisis that has forced the country to shut down all but one of its Danube-cooled nuclear reactors for the first time in 44 years. Continue reading...

title_original: ‘It is not only a future certainty – the disaster is already here’: why we need climate fiction
summary_source: As wildfires rage across Europe and Britain swelters through its hottest summer on record, literary fiction has a vital role to play in capturing the severe consequences of climate crisis Earlier this summer, I travelled through Europe on a book tour. Everywhere I went, the heat broke records. In Italy, Germany and Spain, I sought refuge from the afternoon sun in air-conditioned hotels. In normally temperate Zurich, it averaged 37 degrees. I jumped into the Limmat for relief. On my final day in Warsaw, Poland had never been hotter – one of 14 countries to hit a historic high. In June, when I left to return to the US, Europe was scorching. At the end of July, as I write this, it is burning. Since the heatwaves began, there have been more than 10,000 excess deaths. Yet for many, myself included, the high temperatures brought nothing more than inconvenience – uncomfortable commutes, heat rash, less time outdoors. This seems to be a defining feature of today’s climate crisis; deadly for some, banal for others. Even when the world is on fire, it somehow doesn’t feel like an emergency for everyone. Continue reading...

metadata.summary_zh: 根据国家能源局发布的能源行业新五年规划，中国国内油气供应量预计到2030年将达到4.4亿吨油当量。规划由国家能源局和国家发展改革委联合印发，设定了到2030年新增2万公里长输油气管道、使总里程达到22万公里、天然气储备达到全国消费量13%以上，以及碳捕集与封存项目年二氧化碳注入量达到1000万吨的目标。中国2025年油气总产量创下4.2亿吨油当量的历史新高。

metadata.title_zh: 科罗拉多州气候诉讼案引发利益冲突争议
metadata.summary_zh: 一项最新报告显示，在即将审理的科罗拉多州博尔德县诉埃克森美孚及森科尔能源公司案中，有二十多个向美国最高法院提交法庭之友简报的组织与化石燃料相关企业存在财务关联。该诉讼旨在探讨地方政府能否利用地方妨害法对化石燃料排放造成的温室气体及气候变化损害进行索赔，批评者指责支持被告的组织构成了受油气煤炭企业资助的影响力行动。

metadata.title_zh: 联合国土地大会在蒙古国开幕，以加速推进全球土地恢复与韧性行动
metadata.summary_zh: 来自 196 个国家和欧盟的代表在蒙古国乌兰巴托齐聚一堂，出席《联合国防治荒漠化公约》第十七次缔约方大会（COP17）的开幕式。在为期两周的会议中，各方将就干旱、牧场、农业用地与土壤、资源动员以及私营部门参与等议题展开谈判。目前，土地退化和干旱每年给全球经济造成近 900 亿美元损失，影响全球多达 40% 的土地和 32 亿人口。

metadata.title_zh: 加拿大联邦政府在未出台严格新排放规则的情况下采取行动废除电动汽车销售强制令
metadata.summary_zh: 加拿大联邦政府上周在《加拿大宪报》发布公告，正式推进废除电动汽车销售强制令的拟议法规。然而，总理马克·卡尼承诺用于替代该强制令的更为严格的排放标准目前远未最终敲定，引发外界对减排政策真空的关注。

title_original: The drought burned Welsh fields brown and turned them into an X - ray , showing a 5 , 000 - year - old burial mound , a Roman fort and First World War trenches that no one had recorded

metadata.title_zh: 威尔士干旱将田野炙烤成焦褐色并宛如 X 光透视，显露出无人记录的五千年墓冢、罗马堡垒和一战战壕
metadata.summary_zh: 由于威尔士遭遇严重干旱且降水量极少，航拍图像显露出地面下隐藏数十年至数百年的历史遗迹。这些因土壤水分差异形成的作物标记勾勒出了约五千年前的新石器时代长墓、卡尔亨的罗马建筑遗迹、德甘维高尔夫球场下方的一战练习战壕，以及一处未曾记录的铁器时代或罗马-英国时期农庄。

title_original: Reform’s Tice accused of misinformation after urging people to enjoy heatwaves
summary_source: Nurses, medical experts and green campaigners reject party deputy leader’s dismissal of efforts to reach net zero Reform’s deputy leader has been accused of spreading misinformation after he dismissed efforts to tackle the climate crisis and urged British people to enjoy the warmth of the recent heatwaves. Richard Tice prompted a backlash from nurses, medical experts and green campaigners on Monday after he told a press conference he believed it was “arrogant” to try to stop the climate emergency, while encouraging people to focus on upsides such as better English wine. Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: 英国改革党泰斯敦促民众享受热浪被指控散布虚假信息
metadata.summary_zh: 英国改革党副领袖理查德·泰斯在新闻发布会上敦促英国民众享受近期热浪带来的温暖，并称试图阻止气候紧急情况是傲慢的行为。此言论遭到护士、医学专家和环保人士的强烈反对，批评指出极端高温已导致数千人死亡、数百万次就医并造成重大经济损失。

metadata.title_zh: 地热能潜力巨大：各州如何助力将其变为现实
metadata.summary_zh: 新一代地热能在美国西部拥有巨大潜力，但开发商必须克服高昂的早期钻探成本、投资回报缓慢以及项目开发不确定性等经济壁垒。随着数据中心和电气化带来的能源需求激增，西部各州正通过直接投资和简化审批等工具支持地热产业，但仍需采取更全面的统筹政策，以帮助企业获得大规模基础设施融资。

title_original: Philadelphia neighborhood may finally get some flood relief
summary_source: As climate change makes flooding worse, the city has proposed building a levee, improving stormwater drainage, creating a wetland park, and offering buyouts for the most vulnerable homes.

metadata.title_zh: 费城社区可能终于获得一些防洪救灾支持
metadata.summary_zh: 由于气候变化加剧了洪水灾害，费城东威克社区长期面临暴雨内涝风险。该市与居民合作推出了一系列防洪提案，包括修建土堤、改善雨水排放、建设湿地公园以吸收水分，以及为最脆弱的房屋提供回购计划，帮助居民迁往地势较高的高地。

title_original: England’s ancient oak trees dying in extreme hot and dry weather
summary_source: Woodland Trust says trees struggling in drought stress, with older ‘survivors’ disproportionately affected England’s ancient oak trees are dying in the summer’s extreme heat and dry weather, according to the Woodland Trust, with trees and ecosystems unable to adapt fast enough to the changing climate. The heatwaves across much of Europe this summer have had a notable impact on crop growth and plant health. To cope with the extreme conditions, many trees are undergoing “early autumn”, wilting and losing their leaves early. Crow Leasow oak, Shropshire. Tea Party oak, Suffolk. King John oak, Devon. Enmore oak, Somerset. Lydham Manor oak, Shropshire. Old Knobbley, Essex. Pwllpriddog oak, Carmarthenshire. Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: 英格兰的古老橡树正死于极端炎热与干旱天气
metadata.summary_zh: 据林地信托基金会称，受夏季极端热浪和干旱天气影响，英格兰的古老橡树正面临干旱胁迫并出现死亡。由于气候变化导致生态系统无法足够快地适应，树木出现提早落叶的“早秋”现象，其中老年古树受到的影响尤为严重。

title_original: How soon will the drought be over?
summary_source: Rain has returned to parts of the UK this week but is it enough to end the drought some regions are facing?

metadata.title_zh: 干旱何时才能结束？
metadata.summary_zh: 英国部分地区本周迎来降雨，引发公众关于旱情何时结束的疑问。科学家指出，短期降雨无法彻底解除干旱，水资源完全恢复需要河流水位、土壤水分以及地下水和水库储量经历数月的持续补给。气象、土壤及河流干旱已相继显现，但由于地下水和水库尚未陷入严重枯竭，专家预计需等待秋冬降雨及明年春季的水文评估来判断旱情走向。

title_original: As an industry and a cooking ingredient, seaweed is gaining ground in Brazil
summary_source: - In Paraty, Brazil, a Caiçara family has transformed seaweed cultivation into gastronomy, educational tourism and a source of income. The venture is driven by strong female participation and a deep connection to their territory. - Originally introduced in Brazil to supply the carrageenan industry, the macroalgae Kappaphycus alvarezii is also being used as a biofertilizer and increasingly as a food item.. - Its farming also supports ecological balance. It produces oxygen, absorbs carbon and helps improve water quality by filtering out excess nutrients. - Experts say the expansion of seaweed farming in Brazil faces bottlenecks in credit, marketing, technology and regulation. New research networks and public policies are attempting to organize the sector as part of the country’s growing bioeconomy.

metadata.title_zh: 作为产业和烹饪原料，海藻正在巴西取得进展
metadata.summary_zh: 在巴西帕拉蒂，一个凯萨拉家庭将海藻种植转化为餐饮、教育旅游和收入来源。源自菲律宾的大藻卡帕藻最初引入巴西是为了供应卡拉胶产业，如今也被用作生物肥料和食品。海藻种植能产生氧气、吸收碳并通过过滤多余营养改善水质，但专家指出其发展仍面临信贷、营销、技术和监管瓶颈。

metadata.title_zh: 解读：“超级厄尔尼诺”将如何重塑全球气候
metadata.summary_zh: 全球当前正在经历预计有记录以来最强的厄尔尼诺现象，被许多人称为“超级厄尔尼诺”。厄尔尼诺是热带太平洋地区周期性气候模式的暖相位，它会释放海洋热量至大气中，临时推高全球气温，并重塑全球降水与极端天气，影响数十亿人的生活。本次事件于6月开始，预计将持续到2027年。

summary_source: As utilities switch to renewables, you'll get paid to send battery power back into the system, making it stronger and cheaper for everyone.

metadata.title_zh: 为什么接入所有这些电动汽车实际上可以拯救电网
metadata.summary_zh: 随着公用事业公司转向可再生能源，车主可以通过将电池电力输送回电网系统获得报酬，从而使整个系统变得更强韧且成本更低。一份新报告指出，到 2036 年，加州只要有一成电动汽车车主参与车辆到电网（V2G）项目，就能提供该州长时储能目标三分之一的容量，大幅削减电网储能采购成本。

metadata.title_zh: 每个国家都需要一个模型来帮助优化其能源转型
metadata.summary_zh: 联合国非洲经济委员会执行秘书克拉韦尔·加泰特等专家撰文指出，仅靠国家自主贡献和国家平台无法确保建立安全且负担得起的低碳能源系统。当前全球缺乏将减排意图转化为具体投资的分析基础，为此，每个国家都需要为其能源系统建立一个可落地、全经济范围的优化模型，以明确未来能源系统的形态并计算投资需求与序列。

title_original: On the Great Barrier Reef, management by Traditional Owners is growing
summary_source: - Joint management of the Great Barrier Reef is changing, with Traditional Owners playing an increasing role in the conservation of one of the seven natural wonders of the world. - Despite climate change continuing to threaten the health of the Reef, the World Heritage Committee has again decided not to put the Great Barrier Reef on its “in danger” list, and has cited increased levels of Traditional Owner management in its decision. - Traditional use and management agreements currently cover 43% of the Great Barrier Reef’s coastline and the government has announced new funding and measures to further include Indigenous management. - There are still gaps in the full inclusion of Indigenous communities in the stewardship of their traditional waters, say Indigenous governance organizations, though strides are being made.

metadata.title_zh: 在大堡礁，传统所有者的管理作用正在增强
metadata.summary_zh: 澳大利亚大堡礁的共同管理模式正在发生变化，传统所有者在保护这一世界自然遗产方面发挥着日益重要的作用。尽管气候持续对大堡礁健康构成威胁，但世界遗产委员会再次决定不将其列入“濒危”名单，并在决策中提及了传统所有者管理水平的提高。目前，传统使用和管理协议已覆盖大堡礁43%的海岸线，政府也宣布了新的资金和措施以进一步纳入土著管理。

metadata.title_zh: 为什么仅靠碳市场无法拯救东南亚的特许经营森林
metadata.summary_zh: 新研究表明，东南亚商业特许经营区内仍保存有约 4200 万公顷的完整森林，清除这些森林可能在未来 30 年内释放 12 亿吨二氧化碳。研究指出，按当前每吨 5 至 12 美元的碳价，仅依靠碳市场激励特许经营商保护森林在经济上并不可行，需要辅以绿色金融和生态系统服务付费等更广泛的融资组合。

metadata.title_zh: 萨奇地热公司投运首座新一代地热发电厂
metadata.summary_zh: 初创企业萨奇地热公司在得克萨斯州圣安东尼奥附近投运了其首座新一代地热发电厂。这座 3 兆瓦的中试电厂已成功并网运行超过 120 天，成为美国同类项目中投入商业化运行的第三个系统。

summary_source: Unlimited Potential, a nonprofit in Phoenix, plants trees in vulnerable neighborhoods and helps run a paid workforce development program. The post Phoenix tree planting program grows jobs appeared first on Yale Climate Connections .

metadata.title_zh: 菲尼克斯植树项目创造了就业机会
metadata.summary_zh: 非营利组织 Unlimited Potential 在菲尼克斯易受气候影响的社区开展植树活动，以缓解高温并提供降温阴凉。该组织同时运行一项带薪劳动力发展计划，培训低收入居民掌握树木养护技能，已有约 30 人毕业并几乎全部实现就业，在改善个人生活的同时促进了社区发展。

metadata.title_zh: 问答：什么是“长时间储能”——以及英国为什么需要它？
metadata.summary_zh: 英国正开创性地使用能够长时间储存能量的“超级电池”，以此平抑风能和太阳能发电的输出波动，推进净零排放目标。英国能源监管机构 Ofgem 已确定在新的“上限-下限机制”下支持 16 个长时间储能项目，采用抽水蓄能、大容量锂离子电池及压缩空气储能等技术，预计可在 2030 至 2050 年间为英国节省超过 240 亿英镑的能源系统成本。

metadata.title_zh: 工党称泰斯应就极端高温下的“享受”言论向消防员道歉

summary_source: Discovery marks latest grim finding in lake as water levels in crucial reservoir outside Las Vegas continue to decline Human remains have once again been discovered at Lake Mead outside Las Vegas, Nevada, marking the latest in a line of gruesome discoveries as water levels in the crucial reservoir continue to drop, authorities said. metadata.title_zh: 干旱导致水位下降，米德湖再次发现人类遗骸
metadata.summary_zh: 随着美国西部历史性干旱导致科罗拉多河流域关键水库米德湖的水位不断下降，当局在内华达州拉斯维加斯附近的湖区再次发现人类遗骸。国家公园管理局表示该遗体没有可疑之处，当地法医正试图确定死者身份及死因。近年来随着水位下降，该湖已多次发现遗骸，凸显出气候变暖背景下美国西部严峻的水危机。

metadata.title_zh: LG 在密歇根州开设美国最大的电池单体工厂之一
metadata.summary_zh: 韩国 LG 新能源在密歇根州兰辛开设了一座大型电池制造厂，投资超 20 亿美元，全面投产后预计每年可生产超过 35 吉瓦时的电池单体。该厂除原计划的电动汽车电池外，还调整部分产能用于生产电网储能系统，内政部长道格·伯格姆出席了开幕仪式并对该项目的能源安全意义表示肯定。

metadata.title_zh: 为什么新西兰在应对气候灾害上的支出远多于减少未来风险？
metadata.summary_zh: 根据气候变化委员会的报告，新西兰在适应气候风险和减排方面均未走上正轨。自 2010 年以来，政府针对自然灾害支出的 97% 用于灾后响应与恢复，仅有 3% 用于减少未来风险，这种现状使社区面临更大的损害和成本风险。同时，南但尼丁面临严峻的海平面上升和洪水威胁，保险费用的急剧上涨及潜在的保险退潮也加剧了地方适应气候变化的复杂性。

metadata.summary_zh: 河北港口集团秦皇岛港股份有限公司持续推进铁路运力绿色转型，通过引入采用磷酸铁锂动力电池组的新能源机车开展货物运输作业，实现了生态保护与降低运营成本的双赢。数据显示，该港每台新能源机车每年可减少二氧化碳排放超330吨，节约综合费用超240万元。

title_original: US apartment buildings have tipped toward heat pumps
summary_source: Heat pumps are a key way to get fossil fuels out of buildings — and the tech recently notched a win in the U.S. housing market. 2025 marked the first year that over half the apartment buildings constructed nationwide came equipped with the überefficient electric appliances , according to U.S. Census Bureau data .…

metadata.title_zh: 美国公寓楼已倾向于使用热泵
metadata.summary_zh: 根据美国人口普查局的数据，2025年标志着全美新建公寓楼中有超过一半配备了热泵，这是该高效电气设备首次在全国新建住宅市场占据多数。燃烧化石燃料的建筑约占美国温室气体总排放量的十分之一，热泵的普及有助于减少建筑领域的碳排放，推动住宅供暖的脱碳进程。

metadata.title_zh: 研究发现气候变化导致欧洲海域七月极端高温
metadata.summary_zh: 世界天气归因组织的一项最新研究显示，2026 年 7 月欧洲沿岸海域记录到前所未有的海面温度，人类活动引起的气候变化是导致此次极端高温的主要原因。研究表明，在化石燃料燃烧驱动的全球变暖影响下，凯尔特海、比斯开湾及地中海等区域的海温较历史基准偏高 2.4 摄氏度，如果没有人为全球变暖，这种极端高温几乎不可能发生。

title_original: Without action wildfires in Europe will increase 39% even in best-case climate scenario, study finds
summary_source: Improvements in fire management however could mitigate increases by more than 70%, study shows Wildfires are projected to burn 39% more of Europe by the end of the century even in the best-case scenario for stopping the planet from heating, a study has found , unless action is taken to manage them better. The increase in hot, dry and windy weather that leads to small fires turning into raging infernos is to engulf more of Europe as carbon pollution pushes temperatures higher. In the worst-case scenario the researchers modelled, which would see global heating reach 3.6C above preindustrial levels, the burnt area would almost triple. Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: 研究发现：即便在最佳气候情景下，若不采取行动，欧洲野火也将增加39%
metadata.summary_zh: 一项研究发现，到本世纪末，即便在阻止地球变暖的最佳情景下，欧洲野火焚烧面积仍将增加39%。如果全球升温达到工业化前水平的3.6度这一最坏情景，过火面积将几乎翻倍。研究同时显示，改善消防管理能够将火灾增加幅度缓解70%以上，但无法完全消除影响。

metadata.summary_zh: 中国新发布的煤炭行业规划强调能源安全与绿色低碳转型，但未明确设定煤炭消费量达峰或削减的时间表。专家意见存在分歧，部分观点认为该规划旨在到2030年前稳定而非积极削减煤炭消费，并对继续发展煤炭化学工业表示关切；另有观点则认为，受房地产低迷、工业用煤减少及煤炭进口下降等因素影响，中国的煤炭消费可能已经达峰或将在今年至明年的短时间内实现达峰。

metadata.title_zh: 在更加干燥的世界中，某些传染病却意外地滋生繁衍
metadata.summary_zh: 最新研究表明，随着全球气候变暖和多地持续干旱，所谓的“干旱-疾病悖论”正导致霍乱、西尼罗河病毒和登革热等部分传染病和寄生虫意外爆发。尽管许多水生病原体需要水分，但在水体减少的情况下，部分致命感染与媒介反而通过集聚或生态变化加速了传播。

metadata.title_zh: 今年夏天打破纪录的高温和干旱期间，太阳能支撑了欧洲电网
metadata.summary_zh: 今年夏天欧洲遭遇创纪录热浪与干旱，导致风力发电受阻，核电、燃气和煤电等热电厂因冷却水短缺被迫减产。相比之下，太阳能发电表现超常，结合电池储能满足了历史性高温下的空调电力需求，为欧洲气候适应能源系统提供了关键经验。

title_original: Six things to know about Asia’s heatwave and the health impacts
summary_source: - This year’s extreme weather has been linked to El Niño, which, according to weather experts, could be one of the strongest ever recorded. - Record-breaking temperatures were recorded in South Korea and Hong Kong, and mercury exceeded 40°C in Japan and China. - Apart from heatstroke risks, higher temperatures during El Niño can accelerate the life cycle of Aedes mosquitoes, which transmit dengue, and shorten the time for the virus to replicate, experts warn.

metadata.title_zh: 关于亚洲热浪及其健康影响需要了解的六件事
metadata.summary_zh: 受史上最强厄尔尼诺现象及人为气候变化共同影响，亚洲多地近期遭遇创纪录热浪。韩国、日本、中国及中国香港等地气温纷纷突破 40℃，韩国阳山更录得 42.5℃高温。专家警告，极端高温不仅导致中暑和死亡风险上升，还会加速登革热病毒传播媒介伊蚊的生命周期并缩短病毒复制时间。

metadata.title_zh: 如何培育国家级零碳工厂和零碳算力设施
metadata.summary_zh: 中国工业和信息化部印发通知，全面推进国家级零碳工厂及零碳算力设施建设，标志着该项工作从顶层设计进入实施阶段。通知设置了单位能耗碳排放、非化石能源消费占比、非化石能源电力消费物理认定量占比三项核心指标，并通过科学算碳、源头减碳、过程脱碳、协同降碳和智能控碳等路径，培育绿色低碳新质生产力。

metadata.title_zh: 随着海洋热浪打破记录，各国寻求在COP31上制定海洋路线图
metadata.summary_zh: 由于创纪录的海洋温度削弱了全球最大的碳汇，非洲国家、欧盟、部分拉美国家和小岛屿国家正联合推动 COP31 峰会制定海洋保护路线图。COP31 共同主席国土耳其和澳大利亚正与有关国家合作制定旨在将海洋和气候保护措施纳入区域与国际行动的自愿路线图。专家指出，这一努力可能会受到气候资金不断缩减的掣肘。

metadata.summary_zh: 英国近日由暴雨引发的山洪暴发将在周五有所缓解，周末各地将迎来阳光和回暖天气，但部分地区夜间气温仍然偏低。尽管本周出现降雨，但由于储水量未满，英格利亚和威尔士的干旱形势仍在持续，国家干旱小组已宣布将开会频率由每月一次改为每周一次。

title_original: Proposed London datacentre ‘incompatible’ with net zero with 1m-tonne carbon footprint
summary_source: Exclusive: Planning documents show annual emissions from North Ockendon project would be equivalent to 8,480 flights to New York A “hyperscale” datacentre in outer London would generate more than 1m tonnes of carbon dioxide a year, equivalent to the carbon footprint of 8,480 flights from London to New York, planning documents show. The East Havering Data Centre Campus (EHDCC) in North Ockendon would be one of the largest datacentres in Europe if approved by Havering council, using 218 hectares of green belt to run servers and data storage systems for AI and cloud computing. Its developer, Digital Reef, has described the scheme as “a unique opportunity to create a sustainable datacentre campus of the future”. Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: 拟建的伦敦数据中心碳足迹达100万吨，与净零目标“不相容”
metadata.summary_zh: 规划文件显示，位于伦敦外围的东黑弗灵数据中心园区每年将产生超过100万吨二氧化碳，其全生命周期60年内预计产生超7200万吨二氧化碳当量。该项目由Digital Reef开发，占地218公顷绿化带，全面运营后预计每年耗电26.5亿千瓦时，对英国的脱碳进程构成重大威胁。

title_original: Biggest El Niño for a century forecast to bring UK more autumn rain and storms
summary_source: ‘Unprecedented’ weather pattern over Pacific Ocean to be felt worldwide, with severe droughts expected in some areas The El Niño event developing over the Pacific Ocean is likely to be the strongest for more than a century and make 2027 another record-breaking year for heat, the UK’s Met Office has said. Increased rainfall and storms are forecast to hit the UK this autumn as a result of the “unprecedented” weather pattern, while the pulse in heat it generates means the global temperature will temporarily exceed 1.5C above the preindustrial average, according to the national weather service. Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: 气象局预测世纪最强厄尔尼诺现象将为英国带来更多秋季降雨与风暴
metadata.summary_zh: 英国气象局表示，太平洋正在形成的厄尔尼诺现象可能是百年来最强的一次，并将使2027年成为又一个打破温度纪录的年份。受此影响，英国今年秋季预计将迎来更多降雨和风暴，同时全球气温将暂时较工业化前平均水平高出1.5摄氏度以上。南美洲和西太平洋等地预计将遭遇严重干旱。

title_original: Stormy autumn, cold winter - how might El Niño affect the UK weather?

metadata.summary_zh: 美国严重依赖水力发电，但不断加剧的干旱正威胁其电力供应。由于降水稀少及春季气温偏高导致积雪迅速融化，科罗拉多河流域的米德湖和鲍威尔湖水位降至历史新低，发电能力锐减。同时，加拿大魁北克省也深陷多年干旱，导致输往美国东北部的清洁电力远低于预期，凸显气候变化对北美多地水电供应的严峻挑战。

summary_source: The 10-year blueprint mandates water cuts of up to 40% for California, Arizona and Nevada It’s official: after years of tense negotiations and missed deadlines, there is finally a plan to govern the future of the imperiled Colorado River - or at least the makings of one. metadata.title_zh: 美国有一项拯救科罗拉多河的计划，但专家称这不足以阻止危机

The Guardian spoke to growers across England about how they are adapting to a hotter, drier climate. Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: 布里斯托的西瓜：英国热浪如何影响种植者
metadata.summary_zh: 英国经历了重复的热浪和异常干燥的天气，虽然近期降雨带来些许缓解，但干旱仍在持续且水资源供应需要数周降雨才能恢复。全英多地的种植者面临着付出更多劳作却收获更小作物的困境，五月晚霜、持续旱情以及跳甲等害虫对蔬菜瓜果造成严重破坏，让传统园艺变得不可持续。

title_original: From bone-dry to soaked to the bone, welcome to the age of climate whiplash | Aditya Chakrabortty
summary_source: This punishingly hot and dry summer will probably be followed by another wet winter. But it’s nothing compared with what Britain will endure in years to come This summer could be the hottest , driest and deadliest in English history. Successive heatwaves have so far claimed almost 3,000 lives . Nearly three-quarters of England and all of Wales is in drought, while key reservoirs are parched. Across this brown and stickily unpleasant land, from Grimsby down to St Ives, hosepipe bans are in force , while music festivals are staged not on green fields but in giant dust bowls. Just how bad is it? I asked a leading climate scientist. Aditya Chakrabortty is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: 从极度干旱到浑身湿透，欢迎来到气候剧烈震荡的时代
metadata.summary_zh: 英国正经历史上最热且致命的夏季之一，多地陷入严重干旱并实施禁水令，科学家警告未来极端天气将更加频繁剧烈。未来数十年内，英国夏季将趋于干旱而冬季降雨增多，在干旱与洪涝之间剧烈摆动的“气候剧烈震荡”将对社会和基础设施构成严峻挑战。

title_original: Weatherwatch: Climate crisis fuelling steep fall in migratory bird numbers
summary_source: Many species under threat use the African-Eurasian flyway, one of the planet’s largest mass-migration systems It may still feel like summer, but in the world of birds, autumn migration is already well under way. Cuckoos and swifts have already left us, and while swallows and many species of warbler will not depart our shores until September, many species of Arctic-breeding waders have begun to stop off at our coastal marshes to refuel for their long journey south. This year, however, there could be fewer than usual. A review by the British Trust for Ornithology, working with other international conservation organisations, has found that more than half of these global travellers are suffering major declines in numbers – a worrying downward trend. Many of those under threat use the African-Eurasian flyway, one of the largest mass-migration systems on the planet. Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: 气象观察：气候危机加剧候鸟数量急剧下降
metadata.summary_zh: 英国鸟类学信托基金会联合国际保护组织发布的一项回顾研究显示，超过半数的全球迁徙候鸟数量正大幅下降。在栖息地丧失、疾病和农药使用等多重复杂原因中，气候危机及频发的极端天气事件成为候鸟数量锐减的突出推手。

title_original: Flash flooding risk as heavy rain hits UK
summary_source: Heavy showers and thunderstorms will continue to affect large parts of the UK.

metadata.title_zh: 暴雨袭击英国引发突发洪水风险
metadata.summary_zh: 强降雨和雷暴天气持续袭击英国大部分地区，气象条件导致多地面临突发洪水的风险。相关气象灾害对部分区域的基础设施和日常出行构成了威胁。

title_original: Thunderstorm warnings expire but rain continues to bring risk of floods for UK
summary_source: The prolonged dry spell has come to an end with heavy, thundery showers continuing to sweep across the UK, as Ben Rich explains.

metadata.title_zh: 雷暴预警虽已到期，但降雨继续给英国带来洪水风险
metadata.summary_zh: 英国强降雨和雷暴天气持续蔓延，气象局发布黄色预警并提醒防范道路积水与交通受阻。尽管长期干旱后迎来了降雨，但英国国家干旱小组表示，由于干旱仍在加剧，将把会议频率从每月一次调整为每周一次，并指出需要持续降雨才能恢复水资源储备。

title_original: First ever Fat Marmot Week to kick off in effort to raise money for research
summary_source: Researchers hope contest – similar to Fat Bear Week – starting Monday will be latest wildlife watching craze Monday sees the start of what researchers hope will be the latest wildlife watching craze – Fat Marmot Week. Last winter was tough for marmots living high in the Colorado mountains, where researchers say two-thirds of one population died while hibernating because of insufficient snow cover. Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: 首届“胖旱獭周”活动拉开帷幕，旨在为相关研究筹集资金
metadata.summary_zh: 科罗拉多州山区旱獭因去年冬季积雪不足导致大量死亡。研究人员发起首届“胖旱獭周”在线评选活动，旨在筹集资金以维持因联邦经费削减而面临困难的长期科学研究。

title_original: How a Western Slope Colorado water district is adapting to the drought crisis and looking ahead to build long - term resiliency

metadata.title_zh: 科罗拉多州西部斜坡水利区如何适应干旱危机并前瞻构建长期韧性
metadata.summary_zh: 面对历史最低水平的积雪层和极端干旱，科罗拉多州上扬帕水利区组织当地利益相关者和媒体实地考察扬帕河流域。低流量和高温导致河流水资源危机严重影响农业、旅游业和水上娱乐经济，促使当地各方积极寻求适应极端气候与建设长期水资源韧性的管理方法。

title_original: Carbon pollution has fuelled ‘massive expansion’ of marine heatwaves in Europe, study finds
summary_source: Hottest periods this year in most sea regions would have been ‘virtually impossible’ in a preindustrial climate Carbon pollution has fuelled a “massive expansion” of marine heatwaves in Europe this summer, research has found, with some waters recording temperatures 6C higher than normal. The hottest fortnights of this year would have been “virtually impossible” in a preindustrial climate in three of the four sea regions studied, according to analysis by World Weather Attribution , while in the Celtic region, which covers much of the water around the British Isles, heat hit levels that used to strike just once a century. Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: 研究发现碳污染导致欧洲海洋热浪“大规模扩张”
metadata.summary_zh: 世界天气归因分析组织研究发现，碳污染导致欧洲今夏海洋热浪“大规模扩张”，部分海域水温较正常水平高出6摄氏度。在所研究的四个海域中，有三个海域今年最热的两周在前工业化气候条件下几乎不可能发生，气候崩塌导致了约三分之二的过量热量，对海洋生态系统和沿海地区构成严重威胁。

title_original: ‘A critical crossroads’: who is the woman vying to become the first Caribbean head of the UN?
summary_source: If elected, Guyanese politician Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett wants to prioritise climate issues and ensure the United Nations remains a force for good Don’t already get The Long Wave in your inbox? Sign up here As the Guardian’s Caribbean correspondent, I sometimes encounter stories that everyone is talking about in the region, but are not on the radar of the international media. Today, I’m taking over the Long Wave to bring you one of those stories. This summer, Guyanese ambassador Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett has made history as the first Caribbean candidate for the prestigious post of United Nations secretary general. If successful, she will be the first woman to hold the position too. I spoke to her about the value of the UN, and what a Caribbean leader could bring to the role. Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett started life in the remote Indigenous village of Santa Rosa, in the interior of the Caribbean and South American nation of Guyana. Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: “关键的十字路口”：谁是争夺首位加勒比地区联合国秘书长职务的女性？
metadata.summary_zh: 圭亚那常驻联合国代表卡罗琳·罗德里格斯-伯克特成为联合国秘书长职位的加勒比地区首位候选人。如果成功当选，她将成为该组织历史上首位来自加勒比地区以及首位女性负责人。她表示若能当选，将优先推进气候变化议题，并确保联合国继续发挥积极作用。

title_original: Reform says we need to choose between climate and economy. It's wrong | Larry Elliott
summary_source: The party’s deputy leader Richard Tice says we should stop worrying about extreme heat and enjoy it. This dangerous nonsense will wreck our finances and the planet So now we know: the smart response to the UK’s summer of record temperatures is to do precisely nothing. According to Richard Tice , Reform UK’s deputy leader, the climate crisis is just one of those things. Nothing can be done about it, so we should simply bask in the sunshine. It is reasonable to assume Tice would not have said anything quite as crass had he been addressing people in Stourbridge who have seen their homes burn to the ground . Or the farmers whose crops shrivel in parched fields . Or the firefighters exhausted from battling wildfires across Britain . Larry Elliott is a Guardian columnist Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: 英国改革党称我们需要在气候与经济之间做出选择，这是错误的
metadata.summary_zh: 英国改革党副领袖理查德·蒂斯称应对极端高温毫无用处，主张享受阳光，引发争议。评论认为，这种将应对气候危机与维持生活水平对立起来的观点是危险的，忽视了气候崩溃对农作物、消防及民众造成的真实破坏，且多数英国民众已将极端热浪与气候变化联系在一起。

title_original: Giant whales move into Greenland waters as ice disappears
summary_source: Melting sea ice from climate change has opened up the region for giant whales to undertake "feeding frenzies".

metadata.title_zh: 随着海冰消融，巨型鲸鱼移居格陵兰水域
metadata.summary_zh: 由于气候变化导致海冰融化，格陵兰岛东部无冰海域迎来了大量座头鲸、小须鲸和长须鲸。一项历时数十年的研究显示，这些巨型鲸鱼夏季在该地区进行季节性的大规模捕食，反映出亚北极海洋环境发生了重大的生态转型。

title_original: Zoo boss calls pipeline plan on site 'unacceptable'

metadata.title_zh: 动物园负责人称基地输送管道规划“不可接受”

title_original: 'I have never seen the pond so low in 17 years'
summary_source: James Herd, who works for Surrey Wildlife Trust, says everyone needs to prepare for extreme weather.

metadata.title_zh: “我17年来从未见过池塘水位这么低”
metadata.summary_zh: 英国萨里郡威斯利威斯利康芒的池塘因持续干旱和气象观测超50天无降雨，水位降至近二十年来的最低点。萨里野生动物信托基金会官员表示，极端天气和干旱对当地低地荒原的动植物造成了严重影响，并建议通过引入河狸等自然手段来帮助蓄水应对干旱。

title_original: Watch: Flash flood sweeps vehicle away in Hawaii after Hurricane Lala

metadata.title_zh: 视频：飓风“拉拉”过后，山洪在夏威夷冲走车辆
metadata.summary_zh: 夏威夷遭遇山洪与泥石流袭击，一类飓风“拉拉”掠过夏威夷大岛，造成一人死亡。强降雨和大风将大岛上约 100 栋房屋从地基上冲走，超过 20 万户家庭断电。热带风暴预计将在未来几天继续向西推进，部分岛屿仍处于热带风暴预警中。

title_original: Iraq’s ghost villages: Islamic State drove people away – now a new enemy is preventing their return
summary_source: Nearly a decade after fighting ended in northern Iraq, the climate crisis has brought extreme heat and a water shortage, making life almost impossible The first thing that strikes visitors arriving in Faka, a small village in Sinjar district, northern Iraq, is the silence. No children play in the streets. No shops are open. Roofless houses stretch across the hillside, their walls pockmarked by shellfire, while weeds and wild grasses grow through collapsed living rooms. A decade after Islamic State (IS) swept across the region, war remains visible everywhere. But according to the people who returned, another enemy has quietly taken its place. Rajab Mohammed says the problem in his village of Faka is no longer Islamic State but water and jobs Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: 伊拉克的鬼村：伊斯兰国曾驱逐民众，如今新的敌人阻碍他们回归
metadata.summary_zh: 在伊拉克北部辛贾尔等地区，历经伊斯兰国战乱破坏的村庄如今面临气候危机带来的极端高温与严重水资源短缺。由于缺乏基本服务、重建和就业机会，原本因战乱逃离的居民大多无法重返家园，当地农村生计正陷入严峻困境。

title_original: ‘A new normal’: Miami faces worsening seaweed problem as piles of algae wash up on beaches
summary_source: Officials have had to remove thousands of tons of sargassum from Florida’s beaches amid the climate crisis Dealing with seaweed is the bulk of Chris Bumpus’s job during the summer. As chief of conservation for Miami-Dade county’s parks, recreation and open spaces department, Bumpus is in charge of cleaning sargassum off 17 miles (27km) of county beaches. But some days, the odds are stacked against him and his team. More and more sargassum, a kind of floating brown algae, has been washing up on the beaches of south Florida, west Africa, the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean. Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: “新常态”：迈阿密海滩涌现大量海藻，面临日益严峻的海藻问题
metadata.summary_zh: 在气候危机背景下，美国佛罗里达州迈阿密海滩官员不得不清理数千吨马尾藻。由于海水变暖以及河流带来的氮磷等因素，大西洋马尾藻带自 2011 年形成以来规模不断扩大。迈阿密戴德县每年花费 300 万美元用于清理，仅 7 月份就清除了破纪录的 9000 吨海藻。

title_original: Spotlight on UN desertification summit as it mulls how to spend $12bn war chest
summary_source: Extreme weather has raised the significance of Cop17 talks starting this week on tackling drought and land degradation As swathes of the northern hemisphere bake in what could be the hottest year on record, with wildfires blazing across North America and Europe and heatwaves afflicting millions across Asia, the UN’s bi-annual talks on desertification have assumed much greater importance – and have started attracting more money. Work will begin this week on allocating more than $12bn (£8.9bn) to vulnerable countries to help them deal with drought and land degradation, when scores of countries gather in Mongolia for Cop17. Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: 联合国荒漠化峰会聚焦如何使用 120 亿美元资金
metadata.summary_zh: 在极端天气频发和粮食安全面临威胁的背景下，《联合国防治荒漠化公约》第十七次缔约方大会（Cop17）在蒙古国开幕。各国代表开始着手将两年前承诺的超过 120 亿美元资金落实到发展中国家的抗旱和土地退化治理项目中。

title_original: Not all 'doom and gloom': Reform's deputy leader downplays climate crisis – video

When asked if climate change was real during the Q&A section of the event, the party's deputy leader sought to downplay the catastrophic effects of the crisis, including on crops, animal habitats and human health, amid the extended period of hot and dry weather this summer. Tice suggested people should adapt to the 'changing' climate and celebrate a boom in English sparkling wine UK politics – latest updates Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: 并非全是一片末日阴霾：英国改革党副领袖淡化气候危机——视频
metadata.summary_zh: 英国改革党副领袖理查德·泰斯在新闻发布会上建议英国应当“适应”气候危机，并声称人类“无法阻止”它。在夏季持续的高温干燥天气背景下，他淡化了气候危机对农作物、动物栖息地和人类健康的灾难性影响，并呼吁人们适应变化的气候。

title_original: Ithaca: a scintillating eco-thriller RPG that aims to confront our violent moment
summary_source: The latest game from ‘reality-inspired’ studio the Pixel Hunt sees you transporting precious human cargo – and deciding what to do with it Ithaca has one hell of an opening: Penelope, a disillusioned environmental lawyer, stops her car at a petrol station. But upon returning, she discovers something shocking: the unconscious body of an oil company CEO in her boot, his hands hog-tied together, dangling limply towards the vehicle’s number plate. This tantalising eco-thriller setup is a long way off the typical knights-and-castles fantasy fare of most role-playing games, more How To Blow Up a Pipeline than Dragon Quest . But road-trip RPG Ithaca arrives via refreshingly original developer the Pixel Hunt, a French outfit that specialises in what it calls “reality-inspired” games. The studio has made a number of arresting works in recent years. One was about a Syrian refugee couple making a perilous migrant journey across Europe; another tackled the life-shattering effects of child sexual abuse. The climate crisis was always in the back of Pixel Hunt founder and Ithaca writer Florent Maurin’s mind. After all, he says, it is the uber problem of our day, the problem that touches all other

metadata.title_zh: 《伊萨卡》：一款旨在直面我们暴力时代的精彩生态惊悚RPG游戏

title_original: French PM booed on visit to wildfire-affected region as EU sends assistance to Belgium and Spain – as it happened

title_original: ‘It’s pretty much a guarantee you’ll get stung’: jellyfish keep swimmers off Delaware beaches
summary_source: Beach patrols report hundreds of stings a day as warmer waters and drought create favorable conditions for jellyfish An unusually high number of jellyfish are crowding Delaware’s beaches this summer amid climate change and other environmental factors – keeping some beachgoers out of the ocean and stinging lifeguards as well as bathers. Beach safety patrols in the state have reported hundreds of daily stings as the jellyfish have increased with intensifying environmental factors, including warmer waters, hot and dry conditions, and water circulation favorable to the invertebrates. Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: “几乎百分之百会被蜇”：水母让特拉华州海滩的游泳者望而却步
metadata.summary_zh: 由于水温升高、干旱以及有利于无脊椎动物生存的水流循环等环境因素，特拉华州海滩今年夏天迎来了数量异常庞大的水母。海滩安全巡逻队报告称，由于水母密集并频繁蜇人，每日蜇伤事件达数百起，导致许多游泳者和救生员选择远离海洋，且今年的蜇伤痛感和症状持续时间明显长于往年。

metadata.summary_zh: 英国巴恩斯利市议会宣布计划撤销 2019 年的气候紧急状态宣言及相关净零排放目标，将资源转向一线服务。议会领导层表示将暂停缺乏明确居民收益或财政节省的意识形态目标，但仍会支持具有实际效益的节能降耗与外部资金争取工作。

metadata.summary_zh: 根据欧盟哥白尼地球观测计划的数据，今年 7 月威尔士托法恩的每平方公里野火碳排放量位居全球前列。布莱纳温附近发生了一场面积达 300 个足球场大小的野火，浓烟扩散至 30 英里外的加的夫，引发了当地对儿童健康和空气质量的担忧。

metadata.title_zh: 顶风前行：尽管特朗普发难，工会仍在为美国优质清洁能源工作岗位而战
metadata.summary_zh: 自 2012 年桑迪飓风以来，不断壮大的美国劳工运动开始应对气候危机与经济不平等。国际电气工会成员瑞安·麦克罗恩参与建设了纽约的大型海上风电项目。在气候目标与《通胀削减法案》推动下，劳工领袖致力于确保工人获得清洁能源领域的工会化职业。面对特朗普政府试图放缓能源转型并削弱海上风电的政策，工会表示将坚决回击。

metadata.summary_zh: 在联邦法院作出裁决后，美国环保署被勒令恢复分发总计超过22亿美元、原本旨在帮助黑人及低收入等弱势社区应对气候与环境挑战的专项资金。此前，相关行政当局曾试图终止或撤回《通胀削减法案》授权的气候投资项目。

title_original: If all car tyres were filled with CO2, would this cut atmospheric carbon significantly?
summary_source: The long-running series in which readers answer other readers’ questions probes an intriguing scientific question in relation to the climate emergency Readers reply: Is it inevitable that consumerism will literally fill up the planet? If all the vehicles on the planet had their tyres pumped up with CO 2 , would this lock up enough carbon to lower the amount in the air significantly? Would there be other issues, such as the carbon cost of trapping it all into the tyres? Chris Coldwell, Lancaster Post your answers (and new questions) below or send them to nq@theguardian.com . A selection will be published next Sunday. Continue reading...

metadata.title_zh: 如果所有汽车轮胎都充入二氧化碳，这能显著削减大气中的碳含量吗？
metadata.summary_zh: 英国兰开斯特的克里斯·科德韦尔提出了一项与气候紧急状态相关的科学问题：如果地球上所有车辆的轮胎都充入二氧化碳，是否能锁住足够多的碳从而显著降低空气中的碳含量？同时，这一做法是否会带来捕集碳本身的碳成本等其他问题？读者相关答复和新问题将在下周日公布。

title_original: Can Burnham justify giving the go ahead to oil drilling? Yes, but these must be the conditions | Michael Jacobs
summary_source: Carbon capture and storage could make the Rosebank site compatible with UK net zero commitments – if its owners are willing to pay the price The British government must soon decide whether it should give consent to two oil and gasfields , Rosebank in the North Atlantic and Jackdaw in the North Sea. Amid both insecurity of energy supplies and deadly evidence of the climate crisis, the prime minister, Andy Burnham, is facing pressure from the oil and gas industry and unions on one side, and environmentalists on the other. Labour’s manifesto commitment not to approve new drilling licences offers little help, because the fields already have licences, granted by the previous Conservative government in 2022 and 2023. But last year, Edinburgh’s court of session ruled that the environmental impact assessments on which this decision relied were unlawful. The Conservative government had, the court ruled, failed to include the emissions generated when the oil and gas from the fields is burned. The court allowed work to continue on the fields, but a new assessment had to be done and approval sought again. Michael Jacobs is professor of political economy at the University of Sheffield and a for

title_original: This is not a natural calamity: it is being done to us knowingly
summary_source: Global heating is an outrage, not a tragedy. We deserve the facts about the climate crisis – I choose the Guardian because it’s one of the few places left to share them honestly Climate campaign 2026: help us reach 30,000 acts of support Well, there’s no getting around it now. What many of us once feared has become a reality. The dangerous conditions climate scientists long warned of have become our common, if deeply unwelcome, experience, and season by season, our acquaintance with disorder and extremities deepens. In both hemispheres, wildfires rage right into our cities and incinerate entire neighbourhoods. Marine heatwaves are bleaching corals and cooking seagrasses on a global scale. This northern summer has brought temperatures most Europeans associate with the Australian desert. Heat events in Europe have paralysed whole countries, destroyed infrastructure and killed citizens in their thousands. title_original: Rescue networks built by fire: Saving animals from Australia’s bushfires
summary_source: - While emergency responders prioritized human life and property during Australia’s 2019-2020 Black Summer bushfires, there were few systems in place to protect wildlife or evacuate and care for domestic animals during and after the fires, exposing a gap in disaster planning. - Neighbors, wildlife carers, veterinarians, landholders and volunteers rapidly organized evacuations, rescue efforts, feeding stations and supply networks, demonstrating the power of local knowledge and grassroots coordination. - Fire ecology research suggests animals may be more vulnerable to fire than previously understood, and more research is needed to understand wildlife mortality and survival during and post-bushfire. - Experts say that community-led efforts could dramatically improve outcomes for both people and animals during disasters with better funding, coordination and institutional support. Community networks offer a blueprint for the future as bushfires become more frequent in a climate-changed world.

title_original: Can REDD+ deliver for Philippines’ Iraya Mangyan?
summary_source: - The Mindoro Forest and Biodiversity Conservation Programme combines Indigenous forest patrols, ancestral-domain support, carbon monitoring and livelihood projects to protect more than 40,000 hectares (nearly 99,000 acres) of Iraya Mangyan forest. - Indigenous patrollers and local officials say the program has already strengthened monitoring and helped reduce timber poaching and small-scale mining, while surveys have documented hundreds of plant and animal species across the project area. - Community nurseries and paid conservation roles are creating early livelihood opportunities, but many benefits remain limited and uneven while the project awaits verification, a finalized benefit-sharing agreement and carbon revenue expected no earlier than around 2029. - Whether the program can deliver lasting benefits will depend on finalizing a transparent revenue-sharing agreement, sustaining patrols and livelihoods during the long wait for carbon income, and ensuring the Iraya retain a meaningful role in decisions over their forests.

title_original: Nepal-Tibet flood: this is the cost of not acting in the face of the climate crisis | Sunil Acharya
summary_source: Nepalis and Tibetans must not pay the price – with their lives, livelihoods and money meant for education and health – for global heating caused by wealthy states Sunil Acharya is an international climate policy and just transition specialist based in Kathmandu, Nepal As a Nepali citizen working on international climate policy for more than a decade, it is difficult to look at the harrowing images coming out of the catastrophic flash flood that thundered down valleys in Nepal, sweeping down the Lhende Khola, Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers, and not feel angry. Not just because of the destruction, but because it comes after years of warnings from scientists and civil society that a rapidly warming planet would make disasters more frequent, more intense and harder to predict. This is what the cost of delaying global climate action looks like. title_original: For 50 years, Philip Fearnside has calculated the costs of losing the Amazon
summary_source: - Philip Fearnside has spent 50 years studying the practical limits of Amazon development, beginning with the agricultural settlements built along Brazil’s Trans-Amazonian Highway. His work repeatedly asked who benefits from projects and who bears their longer-term costs. - He produced influential research on deforestation, forest carbon, tropical dams, and the wider effects of roads, often challenging official assumptions about emissions and economic viability. He later contributed to the IPCC’s work on climate change. - Fearnside has paired research with public engagement, publishing in Portuguese, writing for Amazônia Real and Mongabay, speaking to journalists, and testifying on projects including the BR-319 highway. That role has also made him a target of hostility, including at a 2021 public hearing where his microphone was cut. - Former students and colleagues credit him with generous, exacting mentorship and an unusual command of the scientific literature. At a recent tribute at Brazil’s National Institute for Amazonian Research, he rejected any suggestion of a farewell: he intends to keep working.

title_original: The Nepal floods seem a world away – but make no mistake, climate breakdown will affect us all | Nesrine Malik
summary_source: Richer countries might have more resources to deal with catastrophe, but this problem grips the entire planet, however much leaders may want to deny it Climate breakdown is happening on one Earth, but two different worlds. In one, its impacts increasingly encroach on everyday life; longer periods of discomfort and shorter periods of sharp pain. Endless, hotter summers, and within them sudden wildfires, evacuations, homes burned to cinders in a matter of hours. In another, catastrophe. This summer has been a snapshot of that split-screen. The hottest day on record in parts of Europe, and a wave of water, mud and ice in Nepal that so far has claimed more than 750 lives. Thousands of people are still missing. The difference is also one of resources. The climate crisis has an economic cost, but some places can absorb it better than others. Responses to this summer of wildfires in Europe included a rapid scrambling by the French government to provide everything from tax breaks for businesses affected by the fires to relocation costs and aid to rebuild homes . summary_source: In Alaska, the Himalayas, the Andes, Greenland, and perhaps also the Alps, deadly chain reactions are just waiting to be triggered You may not have felt it, but the earth beneath our feet is getting twitchier, and global heating is to blame. As temperatures surge and climate breakdown accelerates, interactions between climate and geology are becoming ever more apparent – as marked by last week’s horrific events in Nepal and Tibet . We still have a bit of a blind spot when it comes to the idea that a changing climate can impact what scientists call the geosphere, but the evidence has long been incontestable. In 2021, a similar deluge ripped through a series of mountain valleys in the Indian Himalayan state of Uttarakhand , severely damaging two hydroelectric power plants and taking about 200 lives. In August 2025, a colossal landslide in an Alaskan fjord created a 500-metre-high wave in an area frequented by cruise ships. A few months earlier, the collapse of part of a glacier in Switzerland’s Valais canton caused a debris-laden torrent that destroyed and buried most of the already evacuated village of Blatten. title_original: Nepal’s glacial collapse foreshadowed a future of climate disaster | Michael Mann
summary_source: The deluge capped a summer of extreme climate events, from deadly heatwaves to wildfires. We must take action now For millennia, the high peaks of the Himalayas were held together by an invisible, frozen cement – permafrost and glacial ice that bound ancient rock into seemingly unshakable fortresses. But as the planet continues to warm, this alpine glue is liquefying. The glacial collapse and deluge in Nepal and Tibet was not a freak weather event ; it was the structural failure of a mountain itself, nature’s latest commentary on the deadly consequences of human-caused planetary warming. And it was the exclamation point on a summer of extremes, illustrating with a sole unnatural disaster the apocalyptic future that lies in store if we fail to take dramatic climate action.
